question:
A 19-year-old woman comes to the office with a 2-week history of left-sided chest pain that intensifies
with deep breathing. On questioning, she reports a minor fall 2 weeks ago but did not seek any medical
care as she felt fine. Physical examination reveals normal heart and lung findings. There is restricted
motion at ribs 6–9 on the left during inhalation. Treatment for this patient's somatic dysfunction should
target a rib with which of the following characteristics? Answer Choices: (A) Anteroposterior gliding

motion (B) Sternocostal joint movement (C) Primarily bucket handle motion (D) Predominant posterior
rotation (E) Primarily caliper motion (F) Primarily vertical displacement (G) Equal bucket handle and
pump handle motion (H) Combined caliper and pump handle motion (I) Primarily pump handle motion
(J) Costovertebral joint rotation
 A. Equal bucket handle and pump handle motion
B. Primarily caliper motion
C. Sternocostal joint movement
D. Primarily vertical displacement
E. Predominant posterior rotation
F. Combined caliper and pump handle motion
G. Anteroposterior gliding motion
H. Primarily bucket handle motion
I. Primarily pump handle motion
J. Costovertebral joint rotation
